newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rate cut to boost Australia - farmers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rate cut to boost Australia - farmers.

text.p: Australia's National Farmers Federation (NFF) said on Tuesday the latest cut in interest rates should boost economic activity.
In its economic committee report the NFF said with the outlook for inflation positive and the economy weaker than expected the Reserve Bank of Australia was correct to lower interest rates.
The central bank cut its overnight cash rate by half a percentage point in July and November, responding to lower inflation and moderate wages growth.
Committee chairman John Watson said at the NFF annual conference the bank was still concerned that enterprise bargaining agreements would create unsustainable wage increases.

"The Reserve Bank will also need to take into account the potential damage to the inflation outlook posed by the so-called living wage claim for across the board wage increases," Watson said in a statement.

The government has said inflation would increase, jobs would be lost and interest rates would rise if the Australian Industrial Relations Commission accepted the Australian Council of Trade Union's (ACTU) call for a rise of A$20 a week for low-paid workers.
"If the Industrial Relations Commission was to grant the ACTU's application, it could account for wage increases of up to 20 percent in agriculture in the first year," Watson said.
He added that if business sentiment and the labour market did not weaken too much then the interest rate falls should provide sufficient economic growth.
The government is offering an A$8 a week rise for low paid workers on awards less than average weekly ordinary time earnings.
Under existing minimum wage rates, some low-paid workers in the metal industry earn about A$350 per week.
